main_text.head: PRÆFATIO.
main_text.p: tanquam à propheta non tan-quam à rege, [?] solidi-tatem ipsius effugii ostendisset: respon-det ad aliud ipsius [illegible, ~9 letters] dicentis Imperatores Christianos, qui Episcopatu suo privarunt, de facto id, non de jure, præstitisse; & abusos eos sua potestate fuisse. Ait igitur solidissimus ille Theo-logus: Itaque nihil est novi cum dicuntur Liberius, Silverius, Johannes injustè pulsi. Nam quis nescit Imperatores sæpè abuti au-ctoritate? Nemo sanus ne-get injustè etiam Athana-

page.notes: The Greek word after "ipsius" is not legible letter by letter; I can make out only "Φύγειον" at its end, so it stays illegible. The "&" before "solidi-tatem" is printed as an "Et" ligature and is doubtful. "Christianos" and "Romanos" are set in a larger italic capital style. "Epifcopatu" is read as Episcopatu with the long s as plain s. "Athana-" continues as "sium" in the catchword position. The watermark "Digitized by Google" is excluded.
